reviewStandard: Scientific identity, morphology, controlled identifiers, caption limits, non-diagnostic framing, provenance, accessibility, and publication files passed the WikiBiome scientific media policy before promotion. The original prompt remains immutable provenance; a separate human output audit reconciles what is actually visible with all published metadata.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI now treats Allisonella histaminiformans as the basionym of Dialister histaminiformans. The original paper describes Gram-negative ovoid histamine-producing cells, but the canonical article instead names unsupported Allisonella hiatal and assigns an incompatible Bacteroidetes identity.
assets.visualReview: No image was generated because a generic historical morphology treatment would not resolve the page's unsupported species identity or obsolete taxonomic framing.
assets.requiredResolution: The control task must correct the canonical article to the current Dialister histaminiformans identity, explicitly reframe Allisonella as a historical synonym, or retire the route. A controlled identifier and corrected scientific scope are required before media review can proceed.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI identifies Alloprevotella as genus NCBITaxon:1283313. The original description reports obligately anaerobic, nonmotile Gram-negative bacilli 0.5-0.6 micrometres wide by 1-5 micrometres long, arranged singly or in short chains.
assets.visualReview: Seven rounded bacilli span restrained short-to-long variation: a three-cell chain plus four singles; no appendages, spores, colony medium, host scene, labels, or disease symbolism are present.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: Seven cellular bodies: one three-cell chain and four singles.

assets.proposedAlt: Seven Alloprevotella bacilli of varied lengths, including three joined in a short end-to-end chain and four singles, on a pale cool field.
assets.proposedCaption: Representative Alloprevotella bacilli. The original A. rava description reports nonmotile cells occurring singly or in short chains with substantial length variation; this reconstruction is genus-level and not diagnostic.
assets.proposedDescription: WikiBiome microscopy-informed reconstruction of the documented single and short-chain bacillary morphology of Alloprevotella rava.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI identifies Alloscardovia as genus NCBITaxon:419014. Primary clinical characterization describes A. omnicolens as nonmotile short, irregularly shaped Gram-positive rods that may show rudimentary branching and are difficult to distinguish morphologically from related genera.
assets.visualReview: Seven separated visual groupings include an attached two-cell pair, a shallow V-shaped branched form, a rudimentary Y-shaped branch, and restrained irregular single forms; no surface hairs, flagella, spores, long filaments, host material, labels, or clinical narrative are present.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: Seven visual groupings, including one attached two-cell pair, one shallow V-shaped branch, and one rudimentary Y-shaped branch; descriptions use grouping language because connected branched forms are not reliably reduced to a prompt-derived rod count.

assets.proposedAlt: Seven separated Alloscardovia groupings, including an attached two-cell pair, a shallow V-shaped branch, a rudimentary Y-shaped branch, and irregular single forms.
assets.proposedCaption: Representative Alloscardovia morphology. A. omnicolens may appear as short irregular rods with rudimentary branching, but molecular methods are needed for identification; this reconstruction is not diagnostic.
assets.proposedDescription: WikiBiome microscopy-informed reconstruction of short irregular and rudimentarily branched Alloscardovia rods.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI identifies Alternaria as fungal genus NCBITaxon:5598. CDC public-health microscopy documents septate hyphae and multicellular obclavate conidia with transverse and longitudinal septa, while primary taxonomic work emphasizes conidial and sporulation-apparatus variation across the genus.
assets.visualReview: A single septate hyphal segment supports a short chain of three olive-brown, obclavate-to-obpyriform conidia with clearly legible transverse and longitudinal compartments and restrained apical beaks; no host or mold-exposure scene is present.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: One septate hyphal segment and a short chain of three multicellular conidia.

assets.proposedAlt: Three olive-brown Alternaria conidia in a short chain, each divided by transverse and longitudinal septa, attached to a slender septate hypha.
assets.proposedCaption: Representative Alternaria sporulating morphology, showing multicellular muriform conidia with transverse and longitudinal septa. Conidial form varies across sections and species; this reconstruction is not diagnostic.
assets.proposedDescription: WikiBiome microscopy-informed reconstruction of septate Alternaria hyphae and a short chain of muriform, obclavate conidia.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI identifies Anaerococcus as genus NCBITaxon:165779. The type-species genome paper describes A. prevotii as an obligately anaerobic, nonmotile, non-sporulating Gram-positive coccus usually arranged in clumps or tetrads and includes scanning electron microscopy.
assets.visualReview: One tetrad, one compact irregular clump, and one pair of cocci are separated and legible; there are no chains, appendages, spores, host materials, labels, or infection symbolism.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: Three separated groupings: one tetrad, one compact irregular clump, and one pair.

assets.proposedAlt: Anaerococcus cocci arranged as a compact tetrad, an irregular four-cell clump, and a pair against a pale cool field.
assets.proposedCaption: Representative Anaerococcus cellular arrangements. The type species A. prevotii is an obligate anaerobic coccus commonly seen in clumps or tetrads; this reconstruction is genus-level and not diagnostic.
assets.proposedDescription: WikiBiome microscopy-informed reconstruction of paired, tetrad, and clumped Anaerococcus cocci.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI identifies Anaerostipes as genus NCBITaxon:207244. The original A. caccae description reports Gram-variable, obligately anaerobic, asporogenous rod-shaped cells.
assets.visualReview: Seven rounded medium-length rods occur as three singles, a loose pair, and one attached two-cell end-to-end arrangement; no stain color claim, appendages, spores, metabolites, host scene, labels, or disease symbolism are present.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: Seven cellular bodies: three singles, one loose pair, and one attached two-cell arrangement.

assets.proposedAlt: Seven rounded Anaerostipes rods, shown as three singles, a loose pair, and one attached two-cell end-to-end arrangement on a pale cool field.
assets.proposedCaption: Representative Anaerostipes rod morphology. The original A. caccae description reports Gram-variable, obligately anaerobic, asporogenous cells; this reconstruction is genus-level and not diagnostic.
